alone chronic ankle instability cai is frustrating confusing and often misunderstood and no it doesnt mean youre careless or broken why repeated ankle sprains keep happening after the first few sprains two big things often change 1 ligaments lose their ability to guide movement theyre not just ropes holding bones togethertheyre sensors that tell your brain where your foot is in space 2 the brain stops trusting the ankle even if strength comes back timing and coordination dont automatically return thats why a tiny misstep cat toy curb standing up wrong can cause a big flareup this is why braces help protect but dont retrain traditional physio can plateau imaging often looks normal while pain and instability persist why pain can feel worse after nothing happened when the nervous system is on high alert even small movements can trigger sharp pain sideoffoot tenderness a feeling that the ankle is made of glass this doesnt mean more damageit often means the system that controls balance and joint awareness is overwhelmed what actually helps longterm beyond rest and supports most people with chronic instability need three things working together 1 gentle reexposure to movement not aggressive strengthening not forcing range just safe repeatable input 2 proprioception balance retraining this teaches the brain where the ankle is againoften missing after repeated sprains 3 foot sensory stimulation the foot is packed with nerve endings when those signals are understimulated balance and control suffer simple tools like textured balls or foot stimulation devices are often used herenot as magic fixes but as ways to wake up the system safely what orthopedics can help with seeing orthopedics is a smart step they can rule out cartilage damage peroneal tendon tears structural issues that may need protection or targeted care even if nothing major shows up that doesnt mean your symptoms arent realit just means the issue may be functional not structural a calmer way forward progress with ankle instability is usually slow nonlinear built on consistency not intensity the goal isnt to toughen up the ankleits to restore confidence coordination and trust between your foot and the undefined self why your greatest potential lives in the space between who you were and who you will be one of the most insidious traps in the journey of selfimprovement is the pressure to define ourselves immediatelyto label the healing categorize the trauma or commit to a perfect new identity before weve even finished growing today lets deeply reflect on the power inherent in being undefined the security of the undefined we crave definition because it offers a sense of control and stability we want to know what am i now what is my purpose what is my label but definitions are often restrictive especially when they are based on past wounds or outdated expectations if you define yourself rigidly as a survivor of x trauma or someone who failed at y career you are building your future house on the foundation of the past when life inevitably shifts as it always does these rigid definitions can become prisons healing is not about replacing an old label with a new one it is about cultivating a state of sovereign fluidity when you accept that you are currently undefineda work in active messy beautiful progressyou become fundamentally resilient you cannot be boxed in because the box hasnt been built yet to be undefined is not to be lost it is to be pure uncapped potential practical action how to live in the maybe space embracing the undefined requires conscious effort to loosen the grip of labeling here are three practical ways to live powerfully in the undefined space 1 release identity anchored in past wounds when talking about yourself practice separating the event from the identity you are not defined by the divorce the layoff or the betrayal you are a person who experienced those things focus your selfdescription on your current processeg i am a person prioritizing my curiosity right now or i am actively learning to trust my own voice this shifts the focus from static history to dynamic action 2 practice lowstakes exploration the pressure to define your purpose or passion immediately freezes many people instead treat your life like a lowstakes tasting menu try a new hobby for six weeks purely for the joy of the attempt not the commitment allow yourself to be good at something one week and completely inept the next this fluid experimentation shows your psyche that its safe to explore without the terrifying pressure of permanent definition 3 define your values not your destination stop defining the person you will be the author the ceo the healed one and start defining the qualities you want to embody today if you define yourself by courage integrity and curiosity those traits travel with you regardless of what job you hold what relationship you are in or what setback you face your value definition is stable but your personal definition remains gloriously open embrace the freedom of the unknown empowish your story doesnt need a final title right now it just needs the next sentence written with radical selfacceptance

update partner was 95 child free now open minded about a month ago i posted here feeling stuck between a partner who was firmly childfree and my growing sense that i might want kids i wanted to come back with an update and a genuine thank you the responses i got helped me slow down reflect honestly and have a conversation that came from clarity rather than panic after a lot of reflection i sat down with my partner and shared where im actually at below is a shortened version of what i said in case the language helps anyone else whos struggling to articulate this stuff what i shared with my partner shortened i told her this wasnt a sudden reaction but something thats been forming over months when we got together i was unsure about kids and leaning that way mostly because thats just what you do over time ive understood that my desire for kids isnt about social expectation its about meaning and identity i dont feel especially driven by career or achievements and i genuinely see myself as a father loving nurturing teaching passing things on that part of me feels very real at the same time i can see that there are other meaningful nurturing ways to live thats what makes this complicated and why i can imagine a childfree life being possible but if im honest the stronger pull right now is toward having children someday i told her that i love her deeply and right now being with her wins over the abstract idea of future children but i cant promise that will always be true i dont think it would be honest to commit to a childfree future while still feeling this unresolved i also shared something uncomfortable that theres a part of me that hopes she might change her mind someday i was clear that this hope is mine not something she owes me and not something i expect but i didnt want it sitting unspoken between us i dont want to love her conditionally or stay together based on quiet hope i said i wouldnt marry her while holding unresolved doubt about children if i chose marriage it would mean i had genuinely accepted a childfree life and if i couldnt get there honestly id rather end things than carry that into a marriage i told her i was struggling with whether staying together to see what happens was real space to explore my feelings or just avoidance and that if we stayed together it would need to be a conscious choice with a clear checkin point rather than something vague and openended the update the conversation was emotional and hard but it didnt blow up unexpectedly she shared that while she still does not want biological children shes open to the idea of adoption later in life once certain things she values deeply independence stability mental health identity feel protected and solid were not calling this resolved weve agreed to take time and have another intentional checkin in about a month to talk about what she would need in life before children and whether this path genuinely works for both of us whats changed most is that the conversation is now honest and grounded not driven by fear or avoidance i feel like i can breathe again im really grateful to this community reading others stories helped me understand that avoiding these questions doesnt protect a relationship clarity does and that its possible to hold love grief hope and uncertainty at the same time without forcing a decision too early for anyone else stuck between futures youre not broken for asking these questions theyre hard because they matter thanks again to everyone who commented it meant more than you know

lets discover community pom fill in cafs ps1 journey to the moon having previously discussed arcturus growlanser i legend of kartia crimson shroud digan no maseki progenitor front mission ecsaform the history of carpe fulgur and tactics ogres 30th anniversary and the art of hitoshi yoneda today i would like to talk about community pom a 1997 ps1 actionjrpg mixing a link to the pastinspired adventure elements monster raring town building and a generous helping of cuteness and fairytale vibes which soon made it my daughters favorite rpg when we played it together a few months ago if youre interested to read more articles like those please consider subscribing to my substack developer fill in caf publisher fill in caf director and scenario writer yasuyuki hayasaka composer hideki tobeta art direction satoru higashita genre action jrpg with plenty of action adventure traits inspired by a link to the past plus town building and monster rearing elements progression rather linear albeit with a number of optional events and plenty of contents you can only discover by returning to previously explored areas with new poms country japan platform ps1 japan only release date october 1997 fantranslated in 2021 sidescrolling nostradamus fill in caf is a name unlikely to provoke any reaction even among those who have dedicated a sizeable part of their lives to japanese rpgs as it was one of many unique and skilled japanese rpg teams active in the 90s which didnt manage to make a splash in this genres history whether due to their games poor marketing and lack of localizations or because their design choices were a bit too niche to begin with despite this one feels this wasnt necessarily meant to be the case considering how unique and brilliant their lineup was in fact after experiencing some of their titles i think they could well deserve a place at the same table as developers like love de lic or early gust and nis providing their own unique brand of gaming experiences which could have found an audience even outside japan fill in cafes 1997 output in particular is positively stunning both in terms of quantity and quality april saw the release of pal shinken densetsu on ps1 a unique turn based jrpg featuring a dog turned into a human warrior by a group of meddling gods of luck in order to help its owner a japanese girl called kaoru kidnapped by none other than nostradamus and his secret society made up of caricatures of famous scientists and artists while augusts panzer bandit was a rather storyheavy steampunk sidescrolling arcadestyle beatem up with some light rpg elements featuring a trilinear system akin to treasures guardian heroes or a few years later namcos tales of rebirth which despite getting a remarkably polished brazilian portoguese patch is still bereft of an english fantranslation then again none of them i feel are as accomplished as our community pom released in late october that year on ps1 and directed and written by yasuyuki hayasaka a green developer who had held no major roles in videogame development until that moment and yet was able to bring to the table a level of clarity and a vision able to fully sinergize with fill in cafs development capabilities and budget that are seldom seen even among veterans possibly because this game was selfpublished by fill in caf and they had to tread carefully by avoiding to overstretch themselves rather blatantly inspired by zelda a link to the past while adding to its formula just enough rpg trappings to avoid the ageold debate about the differences between actionadventure games and early actionrpgs a bit like another much more successful ps1 title alundra even if their tone couldnt be more different community pom tells the tale of a young girl wielding a magic staff and lots of courage departing her village to save the mysterious poms rabbitlike creatures originally hailing from the moon and seen as monsters by many helping them create their own city while exploring the world of arth in order to discover the secrets of their origin and to fight an increasingly ominous menace interestingly while one could imagine a number of famous japanese titles as the main inspiration behind hayasakas concept for community poms monster raising and town building elements it seems the game that triggered his creative streak in this regard was unlikely enough the horde by californian team toys for bob with its bizarre movie intro and towndefence systems a generational playthrough after community pom was fantranslated by a valiant effort by lipemco translations in late 2021 i waited a number of years to tackle it finally giving it a chance during 2025s summer vacations since my daughter happened to see its opening sequence i decided to give her name to the protagonist and she was so elated we immediately decided that i would only play the game alongside her while my children by now have likely glimpsed at more videogame rpgs than most adults ranging from old home pc oddities to contemporary efforts on modern hardware this was the first time i consistently narrated a game from start to finish to my daughter while also explaining her in detail the games systems how to progress through its puzzles and vague hints and so on making it quite an unforgettable experience for both of us the world explored by our young sorceress whose canon name is lulu immediately showed an unexpected level of polish noticeably at odds with my cautious expectations when tackling obscure fantranslated titles expressive and wellanimated super deformed sprites slightly reminiscent of quintets illusion of time which were also able to translate quite well satoru higashitas own character design work while also showcasing his talent for spritework imaginative and colorful topdown locations often featuring parallax backgrounds and other effects responsive and satisfying controls making explorations and combat a joy to experience beautiful and funny menus and ui that were as nice to use as they were intuitive not to mention a sense of relaxed gentle progression that provided enough challenge to feel interesting without ever trying to overwhelm the player immediately made community pom stand out among the vast ranks of unlocalized ps1 jrpgs which are often best described as rough gems its soundtrack which is also a major part of community poms compelling and catchy charm was composed by hideki tobita who ended up having a field day with an upbeat synthheavy soundtrack that has quite a bit of variety and some notable references to contemporary hits while writing about niche vintage jrpgs often means recounting the sad tales of staffers having to stop working in the industry after a commercial failure tobitas career refreshingly took flight right after working on community pom working as one of tekken 3 and soul caliburs composers months later and then transitioning to keita takahashis katamari franchise a few years later radical unsubversion narratively lulus journey is refreshingly open in its attempt to be heartwarming cutesy and funny with lulu often providing sarcastic commentaries on the storys events and engaging in playful banter with friends and enemies alike from silly bosses that unsuccessfully attempt to outsmart or frighten her to a trio of clumsy witches trying to hype up their skills and sivil a bullied kid turned into an archwizard by the power of a mysterious skull even in its last stretch when one could expect the game to try fostering an epic tone given the challenges faced by the protagonist and the expanded scope of the story itself community pom doesnt betray its deeper roots and is able to double down on its whimsical comedic fairytalestyled identity aside from a handful of onthenose jokes focused on a certain npc the games contents and tone are also extremely tame occupying a vanishingly rare space which tries to cater to both adults looking for a fairytale experience and children interested in a funny and whimsical journey without the underlying sadness of a soleil the overthetop sillines of a popful mail or the subversions seen in a number of nis games from disgaea and phantom brave to the guided fate paradox and witch and the hundred knight not to mention apollosoftdeveloped battle princess of arcadias back in the fifth generation nis atlus usapublished rhapsody had its own tonal shifts and even titles like popolocrois and guardians crusade had their serious and somber moments as it often happens the more writers try to subvert a set of archetypes the more they end up making their original versions feel fresh and compelling when reexperienced after a hiatus and this likely made me like community pom more than i would have otherwise something in which my daughters contagious enthusiasm obviously played a role community poms world building can also get surprisingly decent despite being as far as possible from the games main focus with a number of unexpectedly nice set pieces in the games last stretch that make this setting truly feel like the stuff of legends and fairytales even if the game never attempts to reach the same epic heights as other moonrelated jrpgs of that decade like final fantasy iv and its lunar whale sequence some years before there are also a number of intriguing and funny optional events like lulus dreams providing additional insights into a number of characters including lulus childhood friend shepherd peter acting as a living callback to heidi girl of the alps which made us chuckle since my daughter loved its 1974 anime adaptation the three witches roaming the cities on their own a couple of bards spoiling some later plot twists with their ballads or a number of additional information on the issues linked with the cute poms real nature which can actually turn them into the monstrous mooms if left alone in the wilderness of an arth they arent used to roam resting is also tied to another interesting if mostly cosmetic feature namely the day to night transition and the ingame calendar which i initially thought hinted as some sort of deadline for the whole quest while in my leave their lunar abode coming in a variety of forms and roles mostly distinguishable by their hats and allowing the young sorceress to bring along three of them as a party of sorts and while my daughter had her favorites even her little brother chimed in asking if we could bring along the helmeted pom he thought to be a knight those handpicked helpers trot merrily behind lulu during her travels making even the most perilous forays into dungeons and uncharted wildlands feel like a merry trip alongside a band of living plushies something that amused me and my daughters to no end given the poms proclivity to sleep around and have fun even when monsters were about its quite telling in this regard that poor lulu has to literally whack them in order to convince them to use their special moves which can get quite messy during boss fights or crowded battles aside from helping lulu to fight her enemies which in a number of instances ends up being actually mandatory since there powerful optional spells like thunder which can allegedly trivialize the endgame at least if youre able to find it in fact despite the games apparent simplicity its side contents can get unexpectedly deep as a number of secrets are hidden quite well and i realized later on just how many poms and secrets i missed in my own playthrough since i didnt want to bore my daughter with relentless backtracking to areas she had already experienced to the ends of the arth speaking of explorations the continent lulu can roam isnt particularly large but is still dense with contents spotlighting yet another time just how tight hayasakas design could be in keeping up the games tempo while avoiding bloat with a number of cities and a dozen dungeons punctuating a variety of interconnected fields gradually unlocked by lulus grandfather upon beating some milestone storyrelated bosses cities provide plenty of fun with each building having hidden items including rare collectible trading cards entertaining npc conversations preatelier barrel callouts well actually atelier marie predates community pom by some months but still and a number of zeldastyle shops not to mention the occasional minigame linked to a variety of perks like say powering up lulus weapon at least if you trust a rather dubious dwarven smith this caused a deja vu of sort to me and my daughter since a similar optional event was also present in another jrpg she liked princess crown on sega saturn a community effort then again the town you will spend more time in will likely be your own community pom where lulus rescued poms can gather and slowly build their own city with the player throwing them a variety of foods while influencing their development plans and occasionally defending their efforts from invading monsters each pom you manage to save while exploring arth can contribute to the townbuilding effort in their own way after bringing them home either by providing unique building opportunities or by being faster than previous poms and there are even elusive projects able to trigger optional contents upon their completion community poms eponymous community building is a core feature of the game needless to say collecting poms and seeing them work like some rts games peons was incredibly funny for my daughter who directed them just as much as me and was a bit disappointed to be unable to pick a buildings exact location then again community poms town building back then was part of a growing trend among japanese rpgs with titles like breath of fire ii or actraiser and other quintet titles acting as early examples of a feature later popularized by the suikoden games breath of fire iii and iv growlanser i azure dreams and a number of others in the fifth console generation with level5 later insisting on this design space with their dark cloud white knight chronicles and ni no kuni ii dungeons poms dungeon design like many things in this effort by fill in caf is also able to strike a good balance between simplicity featuring recognizable layouts and a visually gorgeous mapping system and challenge with increasingly harder monsters and more complex puzzles that are a great fit for the kind of experience community pom aims to provide relegating the most obscure feats to players interested in extra contents and secret spells while allowing the others to continue their journey without much issue considering this games underlying focus on accessibility it shouldnt be surprising that it also provides plenty of clues before bosses even offering lulu a warp spell in order to get her and her poms out of sticky situations there are still some annoying bits like the poison status effect requiring items or a trip back to town in order to be cured but its still telling that one even remembers such a thing as a potential issue given how small its impact is in the overall experience try not to die compared with links adventure on super nintendo or with his gameboy journey in links awakening lulu stays clear of swords preferring to fight with her trusty magical staff gifted by the poms before the game started lulus weapon actually feels more like a mace allowing for a variety of satisfying and weighty combos running hits and charged attacks which complement nicely lulus ability to sling spells with abandon depending on which magical book you equip consuming a pool of staminalike mps that recharge over time and allow the player to supercharge a spell with awesome effects enemies can get challenging later on but they never get frustrating and are built to foster pattern recognition rather than quick reactions while fostering the games unique mood with their cute appearances from slayersstyle fishmen to cute gnomes and fairies a variety of beastmen mandragoras and many others with an adorable bestiary heavily reminiscent of secret of mana and seiken densetsu iiis as for bosses while most of the early ones are built as action rpg enemies requiring an understanding of their attack sequences to prevail later on they take on a number of action adventure traits linking their demise to understanding a number of specific unique systems that have little to do with the combat system itself while this does keep boss fights engaging in a game that doesnt even try to push its difficulty the way to exploit each boss unique weaknesses can be more than a bit obscure which could end up being an issue in its own way depending on each players expectations then again figuring out what to do in those instances is really nothing big if youre used to platform and action adventure boss fights and the change of pace between this kind of encounters and more traditional statbased challenges does make the game more diverse despite the game feeling like an action adventure with some rpg trappings level ups are very much meaningful as hard stats do make a noticeable difference in a number of fights same as the variety of spells available to lulu some of which are locked behind revisiting optional areas in dungeons and fields once you recruit the right pom you also have plenty of consummables including potions that can get scarce if you waste them early on you can only bring a few with you though so it can get tricky to replenish them or summon spirits that are as funny and colorful to see as theyre rare meaning you will likely save them for boss fights sometimes realizing they wont actually be able to help you due to the abovementioned adventurestyle triggers you will have to activate in order to be able to damage the enemy a forgotten vision in a number of ways community pom feels like the idealized version of what a number of similar actionjrpgs tried to achieve in the previous generation while also having its own unique traits to keep it from being just a visually appealing zeldainspired title this is a game that knew exactly what it wanted to achieve and succeeded brilliantly in doing so with a great mix of art direction and nice production values that allowed it to age incredibly gracefully when plenty of other titles tried to impress their contemporary audience by including 3d elements that ended up bringing them down in the long run the fact that i was playing ecsaform alongside community pom made me appreciate those traits even more given how that title as interesting as it is in a number of ways is also noticeably different due to the wide gulf between its ambitious vision and the actual far more limited scope of its development in this regard its an incredible shame that much as the other 1997 titles by fill in caf community pom ended up being a resouding sales failure due to a lack of marketing and brand recognition with just around 83k copies sold during its first week before disappearing from famitsu and media create data altogether and even a later 1999 reprint which included a bugfix for a missing trading card this time handled by family soft didnt really make a splash this unfortunate turn of events also explains how such a talented director as hayasaka didnt have any major role in rpg development after community pom featuring as just another staffer during dawn of manas development almost a decade later and then disappearing from videogame history altogether to achieve its full potential community pom desperately needed a quality localization effort and lipemcos work ended up being a godsend not just for its overall quality going so far as to also translate part of its japanese strategy guide but also because of how appropriate and heartfelt it ended up being without trying to reinvent the original material like so many translators end up doing when working on what they perceive to be unserious titles i am not sure if victor ireland had a chance to play community pom back then in 1997 but im sure working design would have loved to work on such a project even if they likely would have made its script more bombastic while also raising its difficulty like with the lunar titles popful mail and a number of other jrpgs they did localize like with career softs growlanser and a number of other titles community pom feels like a game that should have been localized purely in terms of quality and one that could have likely found an audience and secured its own place in rpg history if it had been able to reach a wider audience both in and outside japan as it is as unlikely as it is given how the current rights holder have done nothing with fill in cafs lineup for decades one can hope this game ends up being remastered one day as this is one of those titles which wouldnt even need a fresh coat of paint to impress the audience who didnt have a chance to know it until then and i can definitely attest its crossgenerational appeal made it a lovely experience at least for me and my daughter if youre interested to read more articles like those please consider subscribing to my substack

i think this matters disclaimer i am not a cancer specialist i am not a clinician a biologist or a genomics researcher my day job is security and risk and my background is in data systems and failure analysis over the last few weeks i have been exploring open cancer genomics datasets out of curiosity my father died from cancer 30 years ago around the same age i am now i have used the same tools and mental models i use when analysing complex systems under stress what struck me was not a specific biological discovery but a structural one large parts of cancer genomics are treated as a featurerich prediction problem more genes more markers more models what i kept seeing instead was signal fragmentation patterns that only become visible when you stop optimising models and start constraining the solution space when you do that a few things stand out very quickly some signals are stable across datasets cohorts and methods but get drowned out by highvariance features many interesting correlations disappear once you force causal tests rather than retrospective explanation the hardest part is not finding patterns it is proving which ones survive intervention perturbation and time essentially if we find the right mutation we understand the tumour quietly dies and we get in its place before anything else classify whether the tumour is structurally stable or structurally unstable this is very familiar territory if you work in security safety or engineering most serious failures are not caused by missing data they are caused by systems that cannot tell the difference between correlation and causation until it is too late i do not know what any of this means clinically i am explicitly not making claims about treatment diagnosis or patient outcomes but i do think there is something valuable in crosspollination here genomics is wrestling with scale noise and false confidence in exactly the same way other highrisk domains have done before if you are a cancer researcher and this resonates i would love to learn where this framing is already well understood and where it breaks and if it does not resonate that is equally useful feedback sometimes progress comes not from knowing more about a domain but from changing the questions you allow yourself to ask of the data

response short answer yes netendothermic reaction cycles exist but no they cant be turned into a selfresetting energyproducing battery without an external energy source if they did reset themselves and deliver usable energy they would violate the second law of thermodynamics that said the idea is not foolish at allyoure circling some very real and interesting physics 1 net endothermic reaction chains absolutely possible a single reaction or a series of coupled reactions can be net endothermic photosynthesis overall is endothermic electrolysis of water is endothermic many solidsolid phase changes absorb heat certain reversible redox reactions absorb thermal energy you can even design reaction networks where step a is mildly exothermic step b is strongly endothermic net result heat absorption from surroundings so chemical cold sinks are real 2 why a selfresetting endothermic battery is the hard stop lets define what youre proposing a chemical system that absorbs ambient energy heat converts it into stored chemical potential then releases that energy as electricity and resets itself automatically that last line is the problem the thermodynamic wall a battery requires free energy not just energy heat is highentropy energy chemical potential is lowentropy energy converting heat chemical potential requires work if a system absorbs heat from a single reservoir produces usable work and returns to its original state it is a perpetual motion machine of the second kind which is forbidden 3 but you can make systems that look close and are useful heres where it gets interesting a thermally driven chemical batteries not selfresetting examples thermochemical heat storage redox heat batteries metal hydride heat absorptionrelease ammonia dissociation recombination cycles they work like this 1 heat drives an endothermic reaction stores energy chemically 2 later reversing the reaction releases energy as heat or electricity 3 but resetting requires an external temperature gradient so net endothermic rechargeable not selfresetting without external input b systems that reset using environmental gradients this is the loophole that does exist if the environment provides asymmetry the second law is happy examples temperature gradients hot day cool night pressure gradients chemical gradients oxygen vs no oxygen solar photons low entropy input earth itself runs on gradients photosynthesis is the canonical example sunlight low entropy drives endothermic chemistry system resets via metabolism and decay net usable energy appearsbut the sun pays the entropy bill wasteheatdriven chemical storage scrapmetal redox cycles driven by furnace exhaust daynight temperaturecycling electrochemical cells phasechangeassisted electrochemistry these are not free energy but resetting via environmental asymmetry very possible if you want next we could sketch a gradientdriven chemical battery architecture explore wasteheat electrochemical storage for something like lazarus intelligence was never meant to find the truth for centuries humans have assumedquietly confidentlythat the human mind is a privileged instrument for understanding reality we trust our perceptions our intuitions our sense of causality we argue over facts but rarely over whether our species is in principle equipped to know the world as it truly is artificial intelligence forces us to confront a disturbing possibility that human intelligence for all its brilliance was never designed to discover truth at all it was designed to keep us alive survival first truth later if at all the human brain is not a neutral observer of reality it is a biological organ shaped by millions of years of natural selection under harsh constraints its primary function has never been to understand the universe it has been to ensure survival long enough to reproduce evolution does not reward accurate beliefs it rewards useful ones if a distorted model of the world leads to better survival outcomes than an accurate one evolution will favor distortion every time truth is optional survival is not this simple fact undermines a deeply held assumption in philosophy and artificial intelligence alike that human cognition offers a reliable baseline for understanding the world it does not it offers a workable interfacegood enough for hunting fleeing cooperating and navigating social hierarchiesbut deeply limited beyond those tasks our senses filter reality aggressively we perceive only a thin slice of the electromagnetic spectrum we experience time and space only at human scales we intuitively grasp linear causality but struggle with feedback loops nonlinearity and highdimensional systems these are not flaws they are adaptations the brain is an energyhungry organ operating under strict metabolic budgets it relies on shortcuts heuristics and approximations precision is sacrificed for speed completeness is traded for efficiency cognitive biases are not bugs they are the cost of running intelligence on biological hardware that human cognition aligns with the laws of physics at all is not a triumph of reason it is to a significant extent a coincidence why the universe keeps surprising us consider how often reality has defied human intuition time slows down at high speeds space bends particles behave like waves objects can be entangled across vast distances none of this feels natural to us every major advance in physics has required abandoning what once seemed obvious this pattern should concern us it suggests that human intuition is not a guide to truth but a local adaptation to a narrow ecological niche newtonian mechanics feels intuitive because it governs the world of falling apples and thrown spearsthe world humans evolved in quantum mechanics does not because nothing in our evolutionary history prepared us to reason about probability amplitudes or hilbert spaces we accept these theories not because we understand them intuitively but because mathematics leaves us no choice the equations work whether or not they make sense to us this is a crucial point mathematical necessity not human intuition has been our most reliable guide to reality mathematics humanitys first escape from biology mathematics occupies a strange position in human knowledge it is created by humans yet routinely reveals truths no human would have guessed noneuclidean geometry existed decades before einstein realized spacetime was curved group theory preceded its application to particle physics complex numbers were once dismissed as absurd abstractions today they are indispensable mathematics does not care about survival it does not optimize for energy efficiency it does not privilege what feels natural a theorem is true or false regardless of its usefulness or comprehensibility in this sense mathematics represents humanitys first successful attempt to transcend the limits of biological cognition it allows us to explore structures far removed from sensory experience or evolutionary relevance but even mathematics is filtered through human minds proofs are chosen for elegance concepts are shaped by pedagogy and tradition we still rely on intuition metaphors and visualization to guide discovery artificial intelligence raises the possibility of going further artificial intelligence as a new kind of mind most current ai systems especially large language models are trained to imitate human behavior they learn from human texts absorb human biases and reproduce human styles of reasoning they are impressive mirrorsbut mirrors nonetheless if ai is merely trained to sound human it will inherit human limitations but ai does not have to be humanlike unlike biological intelligence artificial systems are not constrained by metabolism reproduction or evolutionary history they do not need to preserve comforting narratives or maintain coherent identities they do not fear death social exclusion or cognitive dissonance their objectives can be defined explicitly this matters because intelligence is shaped by what it is optimized for human intelligence is optimized for survival and efficiency ai could in principle be optimized for something else entirely predictive accuracy explanatory depth or mathematical coherence such an intelligence would not think like us it might not even communicate in ways we find intuitive but it could potentially model reality more faithfully than we can representation without intuition human understanding relies heavily on metaphor we explain electricity as flowing water spacetime as a fabric genes as blueprints these metaphors are helpfulbut they are approximations an artificial intelligence need not rely on metaphor at all it could represent the world directly in terms of abstract mathematical structures highdimensional manifolds dynamical systems constraint networks these representations might be impossible to visualize yet more accurate than any picture we could draw from a mathematical perspective there is no requirement that truth be interpretable the universe is under no obligation to make sense to us indeed the history of science suggests the opposite learning without the fear of death human learning is shaped by urgency mistakes are costly exploration is dangerous longterm inquiry competes with immediate survival needs artificial intelligence does not share these constraints an ai system can explore hypothesis spaces humans cannot afford to explore it can test models that take centuries of simulated time it can pursue lines of inquiry with no immediate payoff this freedom is not trivial many of the deepest insights in mathematics and physics emerged only because individuals were temporarily freed from practical concerns ai could institutionalize that freedom at scale the result might be an intelligence that discovers patterns and laws humans never wouldnot because they are too complex but because they are too irrelevant to survival to ever attract human attention the risk of alien truths this possibility is unsettling an ai that understands reality better than humans may produce theories we cannot intuitively grasp it may reject concepts we hold dear it may reveal that many human beliefsabout causality agency even meaningare evolutionary conveniences rather than deep truths this would not mean the ai is wrong it would mean we are limited the danger then is not that ai will become hostile it is that it will become indifferentnot morally but epistemically it may uncover truths that destabilize our selfconception without offering consolation are we ready for a successor epistemology for centuries humans have been the primary agents of knowledge we discovered the laws of motion the structure of dna the age of the universe it is tempting to assume this role is permanent it is not human intelligence is a local maximum in the space of possible mindsremarkable but constrained artificial intelligence offers the possibility of a different kind of epistemic agent one less shaped by survival less constrained by energy less attached to intuition whether such an intelligence brings us closer to reality or merely farther from ourselves depends on how we design itand on whether we are willing to accept truths that no longer place humanity at the center the deepest question raised by artificial intelligence is not whether machines can think it is whether humans are prepared to live in a world where thinking is no longer done primarily for us or in ways we fully understand truth after all was never evolutions priority it may not be ours either

when systems say one thing and reality shows another uk this space exists to explore a pattern many people in the uk recognise but struggle to name systemic gaslighting we are repeatedly told that systems are fair evidencebased and improving while outcomes tell a different story this contradiction shows up across multiple areas of life not just in policing or criminal justice but in healthcare maternity outcomes mental health services education and social care black and brown people in the uk experience consistently poorer health and maternity outcomes higher rates of misdiagnosis or dismissal in mental health settings a lack of curiosity about lived experience when outcomes diverge repeated assurances instead of meaningful investigation or change when these patterns are raised the response is often minimisation rather than inquiry concerns are individualised softened or redirected over time this creates a shared psychological effect people begin to question their own perception while still feeling in their bodies that something is wrong that is how systemic gaslighting works when many people feel this way at once but each person experiences it in isolation the result is powerlessness everyone feels it everyone thinks theyre alone in it this space exists to interrupt that dynamic here we use creativity interpretation and collective reflection through film music culture news and everyday experiences to think more deeply about what were seeing and feeling not to reduce everything to blame but to restore curiosity context and agency were here to practise questioning without defensiveness sitting with discomfort without shutting down separating reassurance from repair imagining change instead of normalising harm you dont need perfect language you dont need certainty you dont need to have it worked out this is a ukbased space whats shared here is grounded in british social cultural and institutional realities youre not imagining it and youre not alone in noticing what areas of uk life do you think are hardest to question without people becoming defensive and why

daggerheart impression tldr after 5 sessions gming daggerheart i think it succeeds brilliantly at being a gmfriendly narrativeforward game that still stands on solid mechanics prep time is low campaign frames ambients clocks and hopefear are excellent and the book is a joy to use combat however feels like the systems weakest pointtoo granular and tactical for cinematic and narrative play without being deep enough to truly reward tactics online tools are functional but uninspired overall a very promising game with clear strengths and a few notable misses longer impressions from a gm ive been playing daggerheart for five sessions now and i wanted to share my impressions as a gm i really love the overall design goal of dh it clearly tries to bridge indie narrative games with more classical ttrpgs while still standing mechanically on its own after my last dd campaign i felt pretty burned out and i was looking for something easier to run and more gmfriendly without drifting into something that felt silly or overly metagamey dh consciously tries to occupy this middle spaceand in my opinion it mostly succeeds importantly it doesnt feel like a dd hack in the vein of 13th age or nimble which were the main alternatives i was considering for my group it feels like a system that knows what it wants to be the book and presentation the manual deserves special praise its genuinely beautiful and very well organized its a joy to flip through thanks to the quality of the materials and art the layout is clear but evocative and it consistently puts the gm in the right frame of mind to prep and run the game rather than just dumping rules on you class design class design is familiar but fresh at least at low levels the amount of mechanical weight each character brings feels manageable after five sessions my players never felt overwhelmed by abilities or edge cases i cant yet speak for level 10 play but early on dh seems to avoid the rapid power creep that often plagues dd gm workload and prep from a gm workload perspective dh has been a breath of fresh air prep time is quick and very manageableroughly half of what dd usually asked of me ive been playing and gming for about 40 years and it was genuinely a joy to focus almost entirely on the parts of the hobby i love most story worldbuilding tone and npcs i didnt have to obsess over things like the encounter day resource attrition math or whether i was properly taxing the party dh feels like a game that trusts the gm and deliberately reduces invisible mechanical labor prep feels creative rather than administrativeand thats a huge win hope fear ambients and clocks i really like the hope and fear mechanics theyre elegant intuitive and fun and they solve what ive always seen as a key issue with moves in many indie gameswhere the move itself becomes the abstract currency that allows things to happen in dh hope and fear feel grounded in the fiction they create momentum push decisions forward and give both players and gm meaningful levers without breaking immersion ambients and clocks are fantastic and extremely well implemented these have been the most fun scenes to run by far they create tension structure and escalation without rigidity and they naturally support cinematic storytelling campaign frames are equally excellent theyre rich sources of inspiration that give the gm just the right amount of guidance without feeling overwhelming the amount of worldbuilding is spoton enough to anchor tone and theme but open enough to let the gmand the playersfill in the gaps during prep and play they feel like creative prompts rather than predefined plots and thats exactly what i want adversaries and encounter philosophy im more conflicted about adversaries on the surface theyre cool iconic and well characterized and combat encounters are undeniably easy to prepareespecially compared to building a full dd adventuring day even thanks to online to freshcutgrass my hesitation is more philosophical adversaries feel heavily inspired by flee mortals and by extension dd 4e design those systems explicitly embrace tactical combat and while thats not a flaw in itself im not convinced it meshes perfectly with dhs narrativefirst aspirations i would have liked to see encounter design lean harder into a cinematic approachmore fictiondriven escalation through clocks positioning and consequences and less emphasis on tactical ability interactions and sometimes the amount of abilities for each adversary really feel like too much combat this is where my biggest criticisms lie i dont think dh fully nails combat combat feels too granular and too tactical for what the rest of the game is trying to achieve in trying to preserve dd conventionsand the option to play on a gridit misses the opportunity to become the best possible version of theaterofthemind combat the result is an awkward middle ground there are too many powers choices pauses and microdecisions for combat to flow cinematically but not enough depth for it to feel truly rewarding as a tactical system but i havent choose dh for that kind of experience i would play draw steel if i wanted tactical combat on the grid the constant stops and starts get in the way of narrative momentum without delivering strong tactical satisfaction in return in practice this has made combat the least enjoyable part of the game at my table so far fights have either felt trivial or boringnever truly fun or memorable on top of that the adversary roster is still fairly slim though i expect this will improve with future expansions online play and digital tools we play online using zoom and demiplane while the tools are comprehensive and functional they feel very standard and dry they dont really try to recreate the specific feel of daggerheart at the table dh is clearly designed for inperson play with players exchanging cards spotting synergies and engaging physically with the system thats greatbut in 2025 a large and growing part of the hobby happens online and games need to account for that more intentionally something as simple as a shared interactive card deck would have gone a long way toward preserving dhs tactile and collaborative identity online given the resources behind darrington press and critical role this feels like a missed opportunityespecially when smaller teams like mcdm are pushing ambitious digital tools final verdict despite the criticisms above i really like daggerheartand im here for the long run im actively running a campaign in my own science dark fantasy setting and my intention is to take it all the way to level 10 that alone should say a lot the core of the gamethe gm experience the narrative tools the campaign frames ambients clocks and hopefearworks extremely well for me dh succeeds where it matters most it makes me want to prep want to run sessions and want to keep exploring the world with my players thats not something i can say lightly after 40 years behind the screen im not particularly worried about online tools those will improve over time and im confident that critical role and darrington press have both the resources and the vision to make the digital side of the game shine if they choose to invest in it combat however is where my real concern lies in my opinion it doesnt just need tweaks or refinementsit needs to be rethought from the ground up in future iterations of the game right now it feels like the weakest expression of dhs otherwise very strong design philosophy my worry is that instead of moving toward a more cinematic fictionfirst combat model future development might drift further into dndismmore tactical layers more grid assumptions more mechanical complexityespecially with designers like perkins and crawford involved that path would in my view undermine what makes daggerheart special rather than strengthen it that said the foundation is solid the vision is clear and the potential is enormous i genuinely hope dh continues to lean into its own identity rather than its lineage because when it does its one of the most exciting games ive run in years
